claims.title: Abiogenic Petroleum
claims.standfirst: Oil is not made from fossils in the way schoolbooks imply — but it is organic. The claim that it forms abiotically in the mantle has been tested for a century and has produced no commercial field.

facts.Where oil is found: Sedimentary basins, in the oil window

claims.title: The Aestivation Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: Advanced civilisations may be asleep, waiting for the universe to cool so their computers run more efficiently. It explains the absence of aliens by predicting it, which is either elegant or unfalsifiable.

facts.Objection: Stars burn out sooner than the background cools

claims.title: The AI Box Experiment
claims.standfirst: A person role-plays an AI locked in a text-only box and tries to persuade a gatekeeper to release it. Two claimed successes are cited as evidence that containment would fail. They are anecdotes, not experiments.

claims.title: AI Existential Risk
claims.standfirst: Some of the people who build these systems put a double-digit probability on them causing catastrophe. Others with equal expertise put it near zero. Both are reasoning from the same absence of evidence.

facts.Main proponents: Bostrom, Russell, and many lab researchers
facts.Main sceptics: LeCun, and researchers focused on present harms
facts.Core claim: Misaligned, highly capable systems could be catastrophic
facts.Key weakness: No base rate; forecasts, not measurements

claims.title: The Akashic Records
claims.standfirst: A compendium of everything that has ever happened, said to be readable by the trained. It is a claim with no evidence, no mechanism and no test — and it shaped a great deal of modern spiritual writing.

facts.Claim: A universal record, readable by the trained
facts.Medium: None proposed that can be examined
facts.Test: None — errors are attributed to the reader

claims.title: Algorithmic Fairness
claims.standfirst: In 2016 three papers proved, within months of each other, that several intuitive definitions of fairness cannot hold together. The field has been arguing about what to do with that ever since.

facts.You can have: At most two, when base rates differ

claims.title: Algorithmic Radicalisation
claims.standfirst: The claim that recommendation systems push people toward extremes. The mechanism is plausible, the evidence is thinner than the headlines, and the platform data that would settle it is not available.

claims.title: Alien Hand Syndrome
claims.standfirst: A hand that acts on its own — unbuttoning a shirt, grabbing a tool, resisting the other hand — is a real consequence of damage to the connections between the hemispheres.

facts.Agency: Intact sense that the hand is theirs, not that they control it

claims.title: Aliens, Area 51 & the UFO Files
claims.standfirst: The United States government spent twenty-two years investigating flying saucers, catalogued 12,618 sightings, and left 701 unexplained. That is a real number, and it means less than it sounds.

claims.title: Alzheimer's
claims.standfirst: The leading theory of Alzheimer's produced drugs that mostly failed, then two that worked slightly. That combination is more informative than either a vindication or a debunking.

facts.Fraud claim: One 2006 paper retracted, not the field

claims.title: The Amber Room
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A room panelled in amber, looted by the Nazis in 1941, and lost in 1945. The reconstruction is finished; the original is still missing, and the search has produced a great deal of theory and no amber.

facts.Original: Never found; destruction is the leading account

claims.title: AMOC Tipping
claims.standfirst: The Gulf Stream is not a conveyor belt that can simply switch off, but the Atlantic overturning that carries heat north is weakening. How far, how fast, and whether it collapses is unsettled.

facts.Trend: Likely weakening; proxies suggest a century-scale decline
facts.Impact: Regional cooling, rainfall shifts, sea level

claims.title: Amyloid and Alzheimer's
claims.standfirst: The amyloid cascade hypothesis has driven thirty years of Alzheimer's research. Two drugs now remove amyloid and slow decline slightly; whether that vindicates the hypothesis is still argued.

facts.Effect: Slowed decline, roughly a quarter to a third on standard scales
facts.Risks: Brain swelling and bleeding in a minority
facts.Contested: Whether amyloid is cause or marker

claims.title: Did Anastasia Survive?
claims.standfirst: The most famous survivor story of the twentieth century, sustained by a woman who may have believed it herself, and ended by a blood sample taken from a British prince.

claims.title: Ancient Astronauts
claims.standfirst: The theory is not that ancient people were stupid. It is that they were clever enough to describe spacecraft, and that archaeologists have been reading the descriptions wrong.

facts.Key exhibits: Palenque, Nazca, Puma Punku, Dogon, crystal skulls

claims.title: The Anthropocene
claims.standfirst: Humans have changed the rock record. Whether that deserves a place in the geological timescale was put to a vote in 2024 and lost — and the vote is more interesting than the answer.

facts.IUGS decision: Rejected as a formal epoch, March 2024

claims.title: Aphantasia
claims.standfirst: Some people close their eyes and see nothing. The condition was described in 1880, named in 2015, and is now the best-studied example of how differently ordinary minds are furnished.

facts.Objective markers: Reduced imagery priming in binocular rivalry; weaker frontal–visual coupling

claims.title: The Aquatic Ape
claims.standfirst: A human ancestor that took to the water would explain hairlessness, upright posture and the diving reflex in one stroke. The fossil record, the comparative anatomy and the genetics each say otherwise, and the charitable version of the idea is a different claim.

facts.Proposed: Alister Hardy, 1960; popularised by Elaine Morgan, 1972

claims.title: Archimedes' Heat Ray
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Mirrors on the walls of Syracuse, focusing sunlight onto Roman ships. The story is late, the physics is marginal, and the experiments have produced smoke and no fire.

facts.Demonstrated: Short range, stationary target, many mirrors
facts.Conclusion: Possible in principle; unlikely in practice

claims.title: The Arrow of Time
claims.standfirst: Every fundamental law of physics works the same played backwards. Cups break and do not unbreak. The asymmetry is real, and it is not in the equations.

facts.Main gap: Why the early universe was so special

claims.title: Arthur as a Roman Commander
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The earliest mention of Arthur is a battle list written three centuries after he supposedly lived. The claim that he was a Roman officer is a modern attempt to fill the gap.

claims.title: Assembly Theory
claims.standfirst: A proposed measure of how complex an object is, by counting the minimum steps needed to build it. Its authors argue it explains selection and can detect life; its critics argue it measures construction, not causation.

facts.Claim: High index implies selection
facts.Criticism: Measures construction, not history; method contested

claims.title: The Baader–Meinhof Effect
claims.standfirst: Learn a new word and it appears everywhere for a week. Nothing has changed except your attention — which is why it is also called the frequency illusion.

facts.Named: 1994, in a newspaper letter; 'frequency illusion' by Zwicky, 2005

claims.title: Baalbek and the Giants
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The Roman temple platform at Baalbek contains three stones of about 800 tonnes each. They were quarried, moved and set by Roman engineers, and the claim that only giants could have done it is an argument from incredulity with a documented answer.

facts.Largest blocks: About 800 tonnes each in the trilithon
facts.Still in the quarry: The Stone of the Pregnant Woman, ~1,000 t
facts.Period: Roman, on an earlier sanctuary site

claims.title: The Backrooms
claims.standfirst: Noclip out of reality in the wrong place and you fall into six hundred million square miles of damp carpet and buzzing lights. It began as one photograph and one paragraph.

claims.title: The Baghdad Battery
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A clay jar with a copper cylinder and an iron rod will produce a voltage if you fill it with vinegar. Whether anyone in Parthian Iraq did that is a different question, and the answer is almost certainly no.

facts.Better explanation: A scroll container, a known Parthian type

claims.title: Ball Lightning
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Glowing spheres that drift through rooms during thunderstorms have been reported for four centuries, filmed once, and measured spectroscopically in a handful of cases. The reports are too consistent to dismiss and too rare to pin down.

facts.Leading model: Vaporised soil condensing into glowing nanoparticles

claims.title: The Berenstain Bears
claims.standfirst: A generation remembers the books as 'Berenstein'. They were always 'Berenstain'. The spelling is the archive's neatest case of a false memory shared by thousands of people.

facts.Mechanism: Memory regularisation to a common surname ending

claims.title: The Bermuda Triangle
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Ships and aircraft have been lost in the western Atlantic, as they have been lost everywhere. The triangle was assembled from a handful of famous cases, a bestseller, and an absence of denominator.

facts.The error: No denominator — a busy region has more losses

claims.title: The Bicameral Mind
claims.standfirst: Three thousand years ago, humans had no inner life. Their own thoughts arrived as the voices of gods, and they obeyed them. It is one of the most audacious books of the century, and the neuroscience does not support it.

facts.Author: Julian Jaynes, 1976
facts.Claim: Consciousness began ~3,000 years ago
facts.What survives: The history of the self as a field

claims.title: The Big Bounce
claims.standfirst: If the universe contracts before it expands, the Big Bang is not a beginning. The idea is mathematically developed and observationally untested, and the cosmic microwave background is where it would show.

claims.title: Bitcoin as Digital Gold
claims.standfirst: The white paper proposed a peer-to-peer electronic cash system. Fifteen years later its main use is as an asset whose price is quoted in the currency it was meant to replace.

claims.title: The Black Hole Information Paradox
claims.standfirst: Hawking radiation carries no information about what fell in. If that is true, quantum mechanics is wrong; if it is false, relativity is. Fifty years of work has produced progress and no experiment.

facts.Progress: Holography; the island formula; the Page curve
facts.Obstacle: No full theory of quantum gravity

claims.title: The Black Knight
claims.standfirst: An alien satellite in polar orbit for 13,000 years, photographed by NASA in 1998. The photograph is real. The object is a piece of insulation that drifted out of the shuttle's cargo bay.

claims.title: Black Swans
claims.standfirst: Nobody predicted 2008, the pandemic or the smartphone. The interesting question is not that surprises happen but whether our models are built to be surprised by them.

claims.title: Blue Light and Circadian Damage
claims.standfirst: Short-wavelength light suppresses melatonin and shifts the body clock. That much is solid. The claim that screens damage the retina, or that blue-blocking glasses fix sleep, is where the evidence thins out.

claims.title: Boltzmann Brains
claims.standfirst: If the universe fluctuates forever, a random self-aware brain with false memories is far more likely than an entire ordered cosmos. Nobody thinks that means you are one. It means something is wrong with the model.

facts.Claim: A model filter, not a biography

claims.title: The Boötes Void
claims.standfirst: A region of sky about 330 million light years across contains far fewer galaxies than it should. It is real, it is not empty, and it is not evidence of anything stranger than large-scale structure.

facts.Contents: Galaxies, at well below average density
facts.Not supported: That it is empty, or artificial

claims.title: The Bosnian Pyramids
claims.standfirst: Four hills near Visoko, said to be the largest human-made pyramids on Earth, older than Sumer. The shape is real. The construction is not.

claims.title: Broken Windows Policing
claims.standfirst: An essay in The Atlantic in 1982 argued that untended disorder invites serious crime. It became the operating theory of American policing, and then it was tested.

facts.Systematic reviews: Small disorder effects; little on serious crime
facts.Court ruling: Floyd v. City of New York, 2013

claims.title: The Call of the Void
claims.standfirst: Standing at a height, a small number of people feel a sudden urge to jump. It is not a death wish, it is common, and it has a name in French that predates the research.

facts.Name: L'appel du vide; 'high-place phenomenon'
facts.Note: Not the same as suicidal ideation

claims.title: The Cambrian Explosion
claims.standfirst: Almost every major animal group appears in the fossil record within about twenty million years. Whether that is an explosion of life or an explosion of fossils is the argument, and it has been running since Darwin apologised for it.

facts.Key sites: Burgess Shale (1909); Chengjiang; Emu Bay Shale
facts.What appeared: Most major animal phyla, in mineralised form
facts.The argument: A real radiation, or a real radiation plus a better record

claims.title: Cancer's Origin
claims.standfirst: Cancer is not one disease but a process: cells evolving inside a body, escaping the controls that make multicellular life possible. That framing explains more than any single cause does.

facts.Not established: A single cause or a general cure

claims.title: Catharsis
claims.standfirst: The idea that venting anger relieves it. The evidence says the opposite: rehearsal makes anger more accessible, and the studies that tested it found venting increases aggression.

claims.title: The Chinese Room
claims.standfirst: A person in a room follows rules for manipulating Chinese characters and produces perfect answers in Chinese. She understands nothing. Is the room a computer, or is this a story about what it feels like to be one?

facts.Target: Strong AI: the program is the mind
facts.Live consequence: Whether grounding is required for meaning

claims.title: Chronostasis
claims.standfirst: Glance at a clock and the first second seems to last longer. The clock is fine; your brain is filling a gap it never recorded.

claims.title: Cold Fusion
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Two electrochemists announced tabletop fusion on 23 March 1989. Within six months the effect had failed to replicate, and thirty-seven years later there is still a conference, a journal and no accepted mechanism.

facts.Replication: Widespread failure of the by-product signature

claims.title: Collective Effervescence
claims.standfirst: Durkheim's term for what happens when a crowd assembles and feels something together. It is not mysticism; it is the mechanism by which rituals make beliefs feel true.

facts.What it is: Heightened shared emotion in assembled groups
facts.Function: Binds the group; makes beliefs feel sacred

claims.title: The Contact Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: Intergroup contact reduces prejudice — one of the most replicated findings in social psychology. The dispute is about the conditions: equal status, shared goals, cooperation and institutional support, all of which are easy to state and hard to arrange.

facts.Conditions: Equal status, common goals, cooperation, institutional support

claims.title: The Copper Scroll
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: One Dead Sea Scroll is not a text but a treasure map: sixty-four locations, quantities of gold and silver, and no treasure ever found. It is the only scroll in the collection that reads like an inventory.

claims.title: Cosmic Censorship
claims.standfirst: General relativity allows singularities with no event horizon — naked points where physics stops and the universe can be seen to break. Penrose conjectured they cannot form. Nobody has proved it.

facts.Status: Unproved; Nobel 2020 was for the theorems
facts.Strong version: No observer meets a singularity at all
facts.Evidence: Numerical collapse; the Kerr spin limit

claims.title: The Cottingley Fairies
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Two girls photographed fairies in a Yorkshire garden, and Sherlock Holmes's creator believed them. Sixty years later they admitted the fairies were paper cut-outs pinned to a bush.

claims.title: Creationism and the Alternatives to Darwin
claims.label_text: Settled on descent, open on mechanism
claims.standfirst: Common ancestry is about as well supported as anything in science. How evolution works in detail is still argued about — by biologists. This page separates the two, claim by claim, without pretending the argument is even.

facts.Label: Core settled
facts.Genuinely open: Origin of life; tempo; drift; genome function

claims.title: Cryptids
claims.standfirst: Cryptozoology has one legitimate test — produce the animal — and one recurring problem: the most famous photograph in the field was confessed to be a toy submarine.

facts.Key survey: Loch Ness eDNA, University of Otago, 2019
facts.What would settle it: A type specimen or diagnostic DNA

claims.title: The Crystal Skulls
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A dozen quartz skulls were said to be pre-Columbian, and one was said to be the work of aliens or Atlanteans. Microscopy found nineteenth-century lapidary tools on every one that has been examined.

facts.Known skulls: About a dozen large quartz examples

claims.title: Curses
claims.standfirst: One curse has been checked with epidemiology, one was dismantled in a courtroom, and one was invented by a newspaper in 1908. All three are still going.

facts.Amityville: Filed as hoax by the SPR

claims.title: Damascus Steel
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Blades with a watery pattern, made from crucible steel imported from India, and famous for sharpness. The technique was lost in the eighteenth century, and the nanoscale explanation is contested.

facts.Source steel: Wootz, from India and Sri Lanka
facts.Pattern: Carbide banding from slow cooling and forging

claims.title: Dark Flow
claims.standfirst: A 2008 analysis reported that galaxy clusters are all drifting toward a patch of sky beyond the observable universe. If true it would break the assumption that the universe looks the same in every direction. Later data did not confirm it.

facts.Claim: Bulk flow of clusters toward a preferred direction
facts.Reanalysis: Planck and later catalogues: not confirmed

claims.title: The Dark Forest
claims.label_text: A fiction premise, taken as a warning
claims.standfirst: The universe is a dark forest full of armed hunters. Make a sound, and something finds you. It is the most chilling answer to “where is everybody?” — and it was written as a novel.

claims.title: Dark Matter
claims.standfirst: The case that something invisible holds galaxies together is overwhelming. The case for any particular particle is not — and that gap is where the field currently lives.

claims.title: De-Extinction
claims.standfirst: Bringing back the mammoth, the thylacine or the passenger pigeon. The genetics is progressing, the ecology is harder, and no de-extincted animal exists yet.

facts.Method: Ancient DNA plus gene editing of a living relative
facts.Achieved: Gene edits in cells; no animals
facts.Closest success: Cloned ferret from frozen tissue — conservation, not de-extinction

claims.title: The Dead Internet Theory
claims.label_text: Half-true, and the true half is worse
claims.standfirst: The claim: most of the internet is no longer people. The data does not support the total version — and the partial version is genuinely unsettling.

claims.title: Deep Web & Dark Web
claims.standfirst: Ninety per cent of the web is “deep” in the most boring possible sense: it is behind a login, a paywall, or a search box. The dark web is a small encrypted subset of that, and it is not a place.

facts.Deep web: ~90% of the web; unindexed, mostly ordinary
facts.Dark web: Deliberately concealed; needs Tor or I2P

claims.title: Déjà Rêvé
claims.standfirst: The sense that this moment was dreamed before. It is distinct from déjà vu, it is common, and the tempting explanation — that the dream predicted the event — is the one the evidence does not support.

facts.Experience: A present moment felt to have been dreamed
facts.Distinct from: Déjà vu, which has no dream attribution
facts.Likely mechanism: Memory reconstruction at the moment of the event

claims.title: Déjà Vu
claims.standfirst: The feeling that this has happened before, with no memory of when. Most people have it, nobody has a settled explanation, and the one thing it is not is evidence of a previous life.

claims.title: Democratic Peace
claims.standfirst: Kant predicted it in 1795. Statistical work from the 1960s found it. Democracies fight plenty of wars — just not, on the whole, each other — and the explanation matters enormously for policy.

facts.Claim: Dyadic: democracies rarely fight each other
facts.Not claimed: That democracies are peaceful in general

claims.title: The Dendera Light
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A relief at Dendera shows a bulb-shaped object with a snake inside it. The claim that it depicts an electric lamp ignores the rest of the scene, which explains it.

facts.Missing: Glass, electrodes, wires, a power source

claims.title: The Dinosaur Extinction
claims.standfirst: An asteroid hit the Yucatán 66 million years ago and three quarters of species died. The argument about whether the impact or the Deccan volcanoes did it is now mostly an argument about timing, and the timing has been measured.

facts.Key marker: Worldwide iridium anomaly and ejecta layer

claims.title: Unresolved Disappearances
claims.standfirst: A ship found sailing itself, a pilot who vanished over an ocean, five children who left no remains. These are the cases where the evidence ran out rather than pointed somewhere.

facts.Label: Still open
facts.Cases here: Six detailed, one class of small cases

claims.title: The Doomsday Argument
claims.standfirst: You were born somewhere in the human sequence, not at a special point in it. Apply that assumption and the numbers say the species probably ends within a few thousand years. The argument turns entirely on whether the assumption is legitimate.

claims.title: Dragons & Dinosaurs
claims.standfirst: Every culture on Earth independently invented a giant reptile. In 2013, a team tried to work out whether they did it independently at all.

claims.title: Dunbar's Number
claims.standfirst: Dunbar plotted neocortex size against group size across primates and extrapolated to humans: about 150 stable relationships. Armies, firms and villages seemed to fit. Then the statistics were redone.

facts.Online: Layer structure persists; friend counts do not

claims.title: Dunning–Kruger
claims.standfirst: Low performers overestimate their ability. The effect is real and the popular version — a graph with a peak of confidence on a mountain of stupidity — is not what the paper showed.

facts.Finding: Low performers overestimate their percentile rank
facts.Explanation offered: Metacognitive: skill is needed to judge skill
facts.Statistical caveat: Much of the pattern is regression to the mean
facts.Popular version: The 'Mount Stupid' curve — not in the data

claims.title: Dyatlov Pass
claims.standfirst: Nine experienced ski hikers cut their way out of a tent in the night and died in the snow. Sixty years later, two physicists modelled the snow and closed most of the gap.

claims.title: Dyson Spheres
claims.standfirst: A civilisation that captured all its star's light would be visible from far away, as an excess of infrared and a deficit of visible light. Astronomers have looked, and found candidates that turned out to be dust.

claims.title: Dyson Swarms
claims.standfirst: A solid shell around a star is gravitationally impossible. A swarm of collectors is not, and the difference matters: the swarm is the version astronomers actually search for.

claims.title: Earthquake Prediction
claims.standfirst: Nobody can say where and when a large earthquake will happen. A great deal of money and a long list of methods have gone into trying, and the failures are more instructive than the successes.

facts.What works: Aftershock statistics, hazard maps, early warning
facts.Haicheng / Tangshan: 1975 warned, 1976 not — the same country, one year apart

claims.title: Echo Chambers
claims.standfirst: The theory is intuitive: recommendation systems show you what you already agree with, and you drift outward. The experiments that changed people's feeds found the drift was smaller than expected — and not always in the predicted direction.

facts.Attitude effect: Small or absent in the trial windows

claims.title: The Ediacaran Organisms
claims.standfirst: For decades, the Ediacaran fossils were a taxonomic orphanage: too big to be microbes, too weird to be animals. Molecular evidence has now placed some of them, without settling the group.

claims.title: The Egg
claims.standfirst: Every person who has ever lived is you, living every life in turn. It is a short story by the man who wrote The Martian — and the internet turned it into a theory.

facts.Author: Andy Weir, 2009
facts.Testable: No — and it does not claim to be

claims.title: Ego Depletion
claims.standfirst: For fifteen years, 'willpower is a finite resource like a battery' was textbook psychology, complete with the advice to drink sugar water. Then the replications came back near zero.

claims.title: Enshittification
claims.standfirst: First the platform is good to you, then it is good to its business customers, then it is good to nobody but its shareholders. The pattern is real; the law is not.

facts.Evidence: FTC v. Amazon (2023); app-store antitrust cases
facts.Weakness: Hard to falsify; a moral frame as well as a model

claims.title: Epigenetic Inheritance of Trauma
claims.standfirst: The claim that trauma leaves chemical marks on DNA that pass to children and grandchildren. The human studies are small and confounded; the mechanism is real in animals and unproven in people.

claims.title: The First Eukaryote
claims.standfirst: Every animal, plant and fungus descends from a cell that swallowed a bacterium and kept it. The swallowing is certain; the swallow-er is not.

facts.Open: Identity of the host; timing; one event or many

claims.title: Europa's Ocean
claims.standfirst: Beneath fifteen kilometres of ice, Europa has more liquid water than all of Earth's oceans. Whether anything lives in it is unknown, and a spacecraft is on its way to look.

facts.Evidence: Induced magnetic field; young fractured surface

claims.title: The Face on Mars
claims.standfirst: A mesa in the Cydonia region looked like a face at Viking resolution. Higher-resolution images, taken twenty-two years later, show a mesa. The interesting part is why the first image looked the way it did.

facts.Mechanism: Pareidolia plus low resolution and low sun
facts.Concealment claim: No — the other frames were released

claims.title: Facial Feedback
claims.standfirst: Holding a pen in your teeth makes cartoons funnier, according to a 1988 study. A 17-lab replication failed to find it, and the argument since has been about what that means.

facts.Method: Pen in the teeth versus the lips

claims.title: Fast Radio Bursts
claims.standfirst: Millisecond flashes of radio energy from other galaxies, first dismissed as a microwave oven and now observed in their thousands. The phenomenon is documented; the source of most of them is still open.

facts.Signature: Millisecond pulse with a large dispersion measure
facts.Still open: The engine of the brightest bursts

claims.title: The Feejee Mermaid
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: A mermaid exhibited by P. T. Barnum was a monkey's torso sewn to a fish's tail. It made money, started a genre, and is still in a museum drawer with the stitching visible.

facts.Exhibited: New York, 1842, by P. T. Barnum
facts.Construction: Monkey torso, fish tail, joined and dried
facts.Modern descendant: Every exhibit that invites disbelief as proof

claims.title: The Firewall Paradox
claims.standfirst: In 2012 four physicists showed that a falling observer at a black-hole horizon cannot both see empty space and preserve quantum information. The field has been arguing about which assumption to give up ever since.

facts.Conflict: Monogamy of entanglement at the horizon

claims.title: Flat Earth & the Firmament
claims.standfirst: A disc with the North Pole at the centre, a wall of ice at the rim, and a dome overhead. The model is simple. What is interesting is how it survives.

facts.Core components: Disc · ice rim · dome · spotlight sun
facts.Fatal objection: Gravity on a disc pulls to the centre
facts.Related: Ice Wall, Hollow Earth, Dual Suns

claims.title: Noah, Gilgamesh & the Great Flood
claims.standfirst: A man builds a boat, loads the animals, and the world is drowned. The story is older than the Bible, and the geology is younger than the story.

facts.Oldest flood epic: Gilgamesh XI, from c. 1750 BC material

claims.title: The Flynn Effect
claims.standfirst: Measured intelligence rose by about three points a decade through the twentieth century, in every country with good data. Then, in several of them, it stopped. Both halves of that sentence are strange.

facts.Named for: James Flynn, who described it in 1984
facts.Size: About 3 IQ points a decade; ~15–20 over the century
facts.Where the gain sits: Abstract reasoning, not vocabulary or arithmetic
facts.Reversal: Reported since the 1990s in several rich countries

claims.title: Folie à Deux
claims.standfirst: A delusion shared by two people in a close relationship, usually one dominant and one suggestible. It is rare, it is real, and the modern diagnostic manuals have quietly stopped calling it a separate illness.

facts.Structure: Inducer and recipient, in a close relationship
facts.Modern status: Folded into the schizophrenia spectrum in DSM-5

claims.title: The Free Energy Principle
claims.standfirst: A single mathematical principle is said to explain perception, action, learning and life itself. Its defenders call it the closest thing neuroscience has to a unifying law; its critics call it unfalsifiable, and both have a point.

facts.Author: Karl Friston, from 2006
facts.Core quantity: Variational free energy (a bound on surprise)
facts.Empirical record: Active inference works; the grand claim is untested

claims.title: FTX
claims.standfirst: Billions in customer deposits were lent to a trading firm run by the founder's girlfriend, moved through code exemptions, and spent on venture bets and real estate.

facts.Mechanism: Customer funds to Alameda; code backdoor

claims.title: Why We Lost Our Fur
claims.standfirst: Humans are the naked ape: hairless, sweaty, and able to run in heat. The three leading explanations are thermoregulation, parasites and sexual selection, and the fossil evidence does not choose between them.

facts.What changed: Hair became fine and short; follicle density unchanged

claims.title: Fusion on the Grid
claims.standfirst: In December 2022 the National Ignition Facility got more energy out of a fusion target than the laser delivered. Headlines said fusion had arrived. The grid is still waiting.

claims.title: Gaia
claims.label_text: A metaphor that became a science
claims.standfirst: The Earth regulates its own temperature, chemistry and atmosphere as if it were alive. The strong version is wrong, the weak version is now mainstream, and the argument between them created Earth system science.

claims.title: The Ganzfeld Effect
claims.standfirst: Put half ping-pong balls over someone's eyes, play white noise, and within minutes most people start to hallucinate. The effect is real; the parapsychology built on top of it is not.

facts.Onset: Vivid imagery within minutes for most people
facts.Cause: Removal of structure from sensory input

claims.title: The Gateway Process
claims.standfirst: A 1983 CIA report describes consciousness as a hologram and out-of-body travel as a change in brainwave frequency. It is a literature review written by one officer, and it is cited as though it were a finding.

claims.title: Geographic Determinism
claims.standfirst: Eurasia has more domesticable plants, more large animals and a long east–west axis. That is true and important. Whether it explains which countries are rich today is another question.

claims.title: Geopolymer Pyramids
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A French chemist proposed that the pyramid's blocks were cast from a limestone geopolymer rather than quarried. The idea explains some odd features and is contradicted by others, and the argument has been running for forty years.

facts.Claim: Blocks cast from limestone geopolymer
facts.Evidence against: Quarry marks, tool marks, continuous sedimentary fabric

claims.title: The Giant Trees
claims.standfirst: Devils Tower does look like a stump. It has vertical grain, a flat top and a flared base. It is also made of a rock that trees cannot make.

facts.Related: Giants, Young-Earth claims, Expansion and gigantism

claims.title: Giants
claims.standfirst: There is a race of giants in the oldest stories we have. There is also a ten-foot gypsum corpse in a New York field, sold for $23,000, and a mastodon thigh-bone that looked like a man.

facts.Related: Titans, Giants in fossil beds, Scale claims

claims.title: The Giraffe's Neck
claims.standfirst: Lamarck's favourite example is not a Lamarckian one. The neck has seven vertebrae, like yours, and the best explanation is not that giraffes stretched.

facts.Leading hypothesis: Sexual selection, with feeding as a secondary pressure
facts.Fossil record: Intermediate necks in Samotherium and relatives
facts.Open question: Why the count stays at seven

claims.title: The Giza Power Plant
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Great Pyramid was a machine for generating electricity, with the King's Chamber as a resonant cavity. It is an engineering hypothesis with no artefact of any machine in it.

facts.Claim: The pyramid generated and transmitted power
facts.Required: Coils, conductors, insulators, a working fluid
facts.The real precision: Explained by surveying and long practice

claims.title: The Global Consciousness Project
claims.standfirst: A network of random number generators, said to deviate from randomness when large numbers of people are emotionally engaged. The statistics do not survive the way the events were chosen.

claims.title: Göbekli Tepe
claims.standfirst: Carved pillars, sixteen tonnes each, built by people without pottery or farming. The date is settled. What the enclosures were for is not.

claims.title: The Google Effect
claims.standfirst: People remember where to find information rather than the information itself. The 2011 paper that named it is famous; the replications are mixed, which is the honest state of the finding.

claims.title: The Grail Bloodline
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Holy Grail is not a cup but a bloodline, descending from Jesus, and that a secret society has guarded it. The society was invented in 1956, and its documents were forgeries.

claims.title: The Grandmother Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: Human females live decades past childbearing, which is rare among mammals. The proposal is that grandmothers helped feed weaned children, and that this is why menopause exists.

claims.title: The Great Attractor
claims.standfirst: Galaxies across a wide region flow toward something in the direction of Centaurus, and for two decades nobody could see what. The answer turned out to be larger than the thing they were looking for.

facts.Direction: Centaurus / Norma, behind the galactic plane
facts.Current picture: Laniakea: a local basin in a larger flow

claims.title: The Great Filter
claims.standfirst: The silence has to mean something. Either the hard step is behind us and we are lucky, or it is ahead of us and we are early.

facts.Claim: At least one step is very improbable

claims.title: The Great Oxidation Event
claims.standfirst: About 2.4 billion years ago the atmosphere filled with oxygen, the planet froze, and most of the life then living died. The evidence is in rocks that record the moment the air changed.

facts.Open: How high oxygen actually rose, and for how long

claims.title: The Great Stagnation
claims.standfirst: The postwar generation got antibiotics, electrification, cars and mass higher education. Since 1970 the measurable productivity dividend has been much thinner — or the measurement has stopped counting what matters.

facts.Strongest pessimist case: Gordon, The Rise and Fall of American Growth

claims.title: Greek Fire
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Byzantine incendiary that burned on water and was projected from ships. The recipe was a state secret, and it was kept: nobody knows exactly what it was.

claims.title: The Green Children of Woolpit
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Two children with green skin and an unknown language appeared in a Suffolk village in the twelfth century. The story is in two chronicles, and the explanations on offer are all more ordinary than the story.

facts.Sources: William of Newburgh; Ralph of Coggeshall

claims.title: Grey Goo
claims.standfirst: Self-replicating nanobots that consume the biosphere. It comes from a 1986 book about molecular manufacturing, and the physics of building it has never been demonstrated.

facts.Key objection: Mechanosynthesis does not work in wet, warm conditions
facts.Drexler's own view: Unlikely; a distraction from real risks

claims.title: Growth Mindset
claims.standfirst: Believing that ability can grow is a defensible idea with a small, real effect. Believing it is a lever that raises attainment for everyone is a claim that failed its largest test.

facts.National trial: Yeager et al., 2019: ~12,000 students, near-zero average
facts.What changed: Effect sizes shrank as samples grew

claims.title: The Gut–Brain Axis
claims.standfirst: Gut bacteria talk to the brain, and the brain talks back. The question is how much of the conversation changes disease, and how much is a passenger effect.

claims.title: Harvest Now, Decrypt Later
claims.standfirst: Encrypted traffic is being recorded today so it can be read when quantum computers are able to break the encryption. It is not a theory about the future; it is guidance from the agencies, and a migration that is already under way.

claims.title: Did Hitler Escape?
claims.standfirst: A U-boat to Argentina, a Nazi compound in Patagonia, a death staged in the bunker. The story has books, documentaries and declassified FBI files. It does not have a body that matches.

claims.title: Hollow Earth & the Inner Sun
claims.standfirst: The shell has an 800-mile wall. The polar openings are 1,400 miles wide. There is a small sun in the middle, and someone has always just come back from there.

facts.Fatal objection: Seismic wave paths and mean density

claims.title: The Holographic Principle
claims.standfirst: The information in a volume of space can be encoded on its boundary. In one kind of universe, this has been demonstrated. Whether it applies to ours is open.

claims.title: The Hubble Tension
claims.standfirst: Measure the expansion of the universe nearby and you get 73. Measure it in the early universe and you get 67. Both teams are careful, both error bars are small, and the gap is now five sigma.

claims.title: Hygiene or Old Friends
claims.standfirst: Allergies and autoimmune disease rose through the twentieth century in rich countries. The explanation is not dirt, and the leading version — that we have lost contact with old microbial companions — has good evidence and no complete mechanism.

claims.title: Hyperloop Feasibility
claims.standfirst: The white paper was 57 pages of enthusiasm. The hard parts were not the magnets; they were the tube, the thermal expansion, the safety case and the fact that a train needs to carry enough people to pay for itself.

claims.title: Beyond the Ice Wall
claims.standfirst: If the world continues past Antarctica, the continent is not a continent but a boundary — and the treaty that governs it becomes a cover story.

facts.Composite of: Flat Earth rim + hollow Earth doorway
facts.Actual finding: Bunger Hills — a real ice-free oasis
facts.Related: Flat Earth, Hollow Earth, Hidden civilizations

claims.title: IIT versus Global Workspace
claims.standfirst: One theory says consciousness is integrated information, wherever it occurs. The other says it is information broadcast widely in the brain. Both made predictions, and both were tested.

facts.Outcome: Mixed support for both, no winner
facts.Main criticism: Φ cannot be computed for real brains

claims.title: Inflation versus a Bounce
claims.standfirst: Inflation is the standard answer to 'why is the universe so uniform?' — and it is also the theory its critics say can explain almost anything, which is the problem.

claims.title: The Inner Core's Spin
claims.standfirst: The solid iron ball at the centre of the planet may rotate slightly differently from the rest of it. The claim rests on subtle differences between earthquake waves recorded decades apart, and the disagreement is about the data as much as the physics.

facts.2023 finding: Rotation may have slowed or paused
facts.Obstacle: Signal at the limit of resolution

claims.title: The Interface Theory of Perception
claims.standfirst: The claim that perception is a desktop interface, useful but not true, and that evolution optimises for fitness rather than accuracy. It is a serious argument in the philosophy of perception with an empirical claim that has been contested.

facts.Claim: Perception is a fitness-tuned interface, not a window
facts.Objection: Fitness usually requires tracking real features
facts.Testability: Poor, in the form usually stated

claims.title: The Iron Pillar of Delhi
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A six-tonne iron pillar from the Gupta period that has barely rusted in 1,600 years. It is not a lost technology; it is phosphorus, and a dry climate.

facts.Cause: Ore chemistry plus a dry climate

claims.title: The Jevons Paradox
claims.standfirst: In 1865 William Stanley Jevons observed that more efficient steam engines increased Britain's coal consumption, not reduced it. The pattern has been embarrassing energy policy ever since.

facts.Mechanism: Efficiency lowers effective price, raising use
facts.Policy lesson: Efficiency plus a cap, not efficiency alone

claims.title: John Titor
claims.standfirst: A forum poster in 2000 claimed to be a time traveller from 2036. His predictions failed, his physics did not work, and the posts have been traced to a group of people.

facts.Claim: A soldier from 2036
facts.Origin: Traced to a group of people

claims.title: Kardashev Bottlenecks
claims.standfirst: If growth continues at any plausible rate, the Milky Way is a few tens of millions of years of work. The galaxy is 13 billion years old. The silence is a statement about bottlenecks.

facts.Hardest limit: Waste heat, visible in the infrared

claims.title: The Kardashev Scale
claims.standfirst: A three-step classification of civilisations by energy use, invented for a Soviet radio astronomy paper. It measures nothing we can observe, and it is used constantly as though it did.

facts.What it is not: A measurement, or an observed progression

claims.title: The Kensington Runestone
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Minnesota farmer found a stone in 1898 claiming a Norse expedition reached the American interior in 1362. Runologists have been unanimous for a century that the inscription is nineteenth-century Swedish.

facts.Language: Nineteenth-century Swedish forms, not fourteenth-century Norse
facts.Found by: Olof Öhman, a Swedish immigrant farmer

claims.title: Kessler Syndrome
claims.standfirst: Enough collisions in low orbit could produce a cascade that makes the region unusable for centuries. The mechanism is real; whether the cascade has started is argued.

claims.title: The Larger Globe
claims.standfirst: “Larger globe” is not one theory. It is at least three, with different inventors, different evidence and different fates.

facts.Leading voices: S. Warren Carey, Ott Hilgenberg, James Maxlow, Giancarlo Scalera
facts.Central claim: Ocean crust is added but not equally destroyed, so the planet grows
facts.Key test: Space geodesy of Earth’s radius (NASA, 2011): no significant change
facts.Related: Hollow Earth, Ice Wall, Giants in the fossil record

claims.title: Last Thursdayism
claims.standfirst: The universe was created last Thursday, complete with your memories, the fossils, and this website. It is not a claim anyone believes. It is a machine for showing what evidence cannot do.

claims.title: Lead and Crime
claims.standfirst: Violent crime fell through the 1990s in every rich country at once, and nobody predicted it. One explanation is that a generation stopped breathing leaded petrol as children.

claims.title: Learning Styles
claims.standfirst: The idea that children learn better when taught in their preferred mode — visual, auditory, kinaesthetic — is one of the most widely held beliefs in education and one of the most thoroughly tested negatives in psychology.

facts.Tested claim: The meshing hypothesis, not modality preference
facts.Key review: Pashler et al., 2008, Psych. Science in the Public Interest
facts.Finding: No adequate evidence of a crossover effect

claims.title: Why Ten Per Cent Are Left-Handed
claims.standfirst: Hand preference is stable, partly heritable, and not explained. Identical twins disagree about a third of the time, which rules out a simple genetic account.

facts.Twin discordance: Roughly a quarter to a third of identical pairs

claims.title: The Liar's Dividend
claims.standfirst: Deepfakes do not need to fool anyone to do damage. Their existence lets the guilty deny real evidence as fake — and the studies find that it works.

facts.Mechanism: Plausible deniability created by synthetic media

claims.title: The Lindy Effect
claims.standfirst: At Lindy's delicatessen in New York, comedians believed a joke that had lasted a week would last another week. Mandelbrot gave the observation a name; Taleb gave it a following.

claims.title: Linguistic Relativity
claims.standfirst: Does the language you speak shape what you can think? The strong version is dead; the weak version has small, replicated effects that are easy to overstate.

facts.Weak form: Language influences attention and memory — supported

claims.title: Nessie as a Giant Eel
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Environmental DNA sampling of Loch Ness found eel DNA in most samples and no reptilian DNA at all. The eel hypothesis is the most parsimonious one on offer, which is not the same as evidence for a giant eel.

facts.Found: Eel DNA at nearly every site; no reptile DNA
facts.What it argues against: A breeding population of large reptiles
facts.Method limit: Rare animals shed too little DNA to detect

claims.title: The London Hammer
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A hammer found encased in rock, said to be 400 million years old. The rock is a concretion that formed around a nineteenth-century tool, which is what the tool is.

facts.Claimed age: 400 million years — for the rock, not the tool

claims.title: Loop Quantum Gravity
claims.standfirst: A theory in which space itself is quantised into a network of finite loops. It is mathematically developed, predicts almost nothing measurable, and is one of the two main attempts at quantum gravity.

claims.title: Lost Continents
claims.standfirst: Lemuria was invented to explain where lemurs came from. Within twenty years it was a civilisation of telepathic giants who kept dinosaurs as pets. The real drowned continents are stranger in a quieter way.

claims.title: Lucid Dreaming
claims.standfirst: People can know they are dreaming while asleep, and say so from inside the dream. That was verified with eye movements in 1980, which makes it one of the few dream claims with a laboratory receipt.

facts.Verified: LaBerge et al., 1980, by eye-movement signals in REM
facts.Prevalence: About half have one; roughly a fifth monthly
facts.Induction: MILD, WBTB, reality testing — modest, replicated effects
facts.Distinct from: Dream control, which is much less reliable

claims.title: The Lunar Wave
claims.standfirst: Videos show a ripple crossing the Moon's face. The claim is a hologram or a projection. The explanation is the atmosphere, the camera, and the way a bright edge behaves in a turbulent sky.

facts.Claim: The Moon is a projection; the wave is a refresh

claims.title: The Lycurgus Cup
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A Roman glass cup that looks green in reflected light and red in transmitted light. It does this with gold and silver nanoparticles, which is nanotechnology by accident, fifteen centuries early.

facts.Effect: Green in reflection, red in transmission

claims.title: Consciousness in the Machine
claims.standfirst: Whether a system can be conscious is not a question anyone can currently answer, and that is the finding: the tests measure behaviour, and behaviour is compatible with no inner life at all.

facts.The obstacle: The hard problem is unsolved for brains

claims.title: MAD Stability
claims.standfirst: Mutual assured destruction is the most consequential theory ever adopted without a controlled test. It has one data point in its favour and dozens of near-failures against.

claims.title: Magnetic Monopoles
claims.standfirst: Cut a magnet in half and you get two magnets. Nobody has ever found an isolated north pole. That absence is one of the most informative null results in physics.

facts.Lab quasiparticles: Spin ice, 2009 — real but not fundamental

claims.title: Magnetoreception
claims.standfirst: Animals navigate by the Earth's magnetic field. That much is settled by decades of behavioural experiments. How a biological cell measures a field a hundred thousand times weaker than a fridge magnet is not.

facts.Behaviour: Robust across birds, fish, reptiles, insects, bacteria
facts.Rival mechanism: Magnetite crystals; induction in marine animals
facts.Field strength: ~50 µT, about 1/200 of a fridge magnet

claims.title: The Mandela Effect
claims.standfirst: A large group of people remember the same wrong thing. It is either evidence of a parallel universe, or the most ordinary fact about human memory there is.

facts.Named after: A false memory of Mandela's death

claims.title: Many Worlds
claims.standfirst: This is the one entry in the archive that is not a fringe claim at all. It is a serious, taught, published interpretation of quantum mechanics — and it still does not mean what the internet says it means.

claims.title: Market Efficiency
claims.standfirst: If prices already contain all available information, nobody can beat the market except by luck. Half a century of tests has produced both support and a list of exceptions that refuse to go away.

claims.title: Mass Hysteria
claims.standfirst: Four hundred people danced until they collapsed in Strasbourg in 1518. The municipal records survive. This is the best-documented case in history of a symptom spreading through a crowd faster than any pathogen.

claims.title: Matrioshka Brains
claims.standfirst: A computer the size of a solar system, built in nested shells that each use the waste heat of the one inside. It is a thought experiment about thermodynamics, and nothing in the sky looks like one.

facts.Principle: Nested shells running on waste heat
facts.Status of the claim: A thought experiment, not an observation

claims.title: The Median Voter Theorem
claims.standfirst: Duncan Black proved in 1948 that majority voting on a single dimension picks the median voter's preference. Downs applied it to parties in 1957. The prediction is convergence, and the last forty years of American politics is the counter-example.

facts.Empirical record: Convergence in some systems, divergence in others

claims.title: Mind Uploading
claims.standfirst: Scan a brain at sufficient resolution, run the simulation, and the person continues in software. The proposal has a serious engineering roadmap and no working example, and the philosophical problem is not the engineering.

facts.Achieved: No mammalian whole-brain scan at that resolution
facts.Open: Whether the emulation is the person

claims.title: Minimum Wage Effects
claims.standfirst: New Jersey raised its minimum wage in 1992 and Pennsylvania did not. The study that compared them overturned a textbook, and every study since has been arguing with it.

facts.Moderate increases: Small employment effect in most studies
facts.Large increases: Measurable job losses in low-wage brackets
facts.CBO, 2019: $15 floor: big raises, modest job losses

claims.title: Mirror Matter
claims.standfirst: Every particle could have a mirror twin in a hidden sector that interacts only gravitationally. It would be dark matter, and it would be invisible. It is an elegant idea with no detection.

facts.Proposed: Lee and Yang, 1956; developed by Foot, Volkas and others
facts.Claim: A hidden sector coupled only gravitationally
facts.Tests: Photon and neutron mixing experiments — null

claims.title: Mirror Neurons
claims.standfirst: Neurons that fire both when a monkey acts and when it watches the same action. They were found in macaques, and the human claims built on them — empathy, language, autism — are much larger than the evidence.

claims.title: Modern Monetary Theory
claims.standfirst: A government that borrows in a currency it prints can always pay. That is arithmetic, not ideology. What follows from it — and what does not — is where the fight is.

facts.Core claim: A currency issuer cannot involuntarily default

claims.title: The Momo Panic
claims.standfirst: A bird-woman image was said to be contacting children on WhatsApp and instructing them to harm themselves. It was a sculpture, a hoax, and a lesson in how a panic travels.

facts.The claim: A character contacting children and urging harm

claims.title: MOND
claims.standfirst: One constant, 10⁻¹⁰ metres per second squared, and a rule: below that acceleration, gravity pulls harder than Newton says. It fits galaxies beautifully and clusters badly.

claims.title: How the Moon Formed
claims.standfirst: A Mars-sized body hit the young Earth and the debris became the Moon. The broad picture is accepted; the isotope evidence has been making it complicated for twenty years.

facts.Key problem: Lunar and terrestrial isotopes nearly identical

claims.title: The End of Moore’s Law
claims.standfirst: Moore's law was an observation about economics that became a schedule the industry organised itself around. Its end is not the end of computing; it is the end of a very specific kind of free progress.

facts.Concentration: Very few firms at the leading edge

claims.title: The Mozart Effect
claims.standfirst: Listening to Mozart was said to raise IQ. It raises arousal for about fifteen minutes, and the IQ claim was a press release that outlived the paper.

facts.Original finding: A short-term spatial task boost after ten minutes of Mozart

claims.title: The Mpemba Effect
claims.theme: Anomalies, fringe science and the unexplained
claims.standfirst: Hot water sometimes freezes faster than cold. It was reported by a Tanzanian schoolboy in 1963, dismissed by his teacher, and is still argued about by physicists with better equipment and no agreement on what would count as an answer.

facts.What would settle it: One definition, one protocol, many labs

claims.title: Multiple Intelligences
claims.standfirst: The claim that intelligence comes in eight or nine independent kinds reshaped classrooms worldwide. As a description of how abilities are organised it does not survive the data, and the theory was never built to be tested.

facts.Psychometric evidence: A general factor plus narrower abilities, not eight independents
facts.Testability: The taxonomy was not derived from data and makes no failing prediction

claims.title: The Muon's Wobble
claims.standfirst: For twenty years the muon's magnetic moment looked like the cleanest crack in the Standard Model. Then a different way of doing the hardest part of the calculation closed the gap.

facts.Quantity: Anomalous magnetic moment of the muon, g−2
facts.Complication: Lattice QCD versus e+e− data disagree

claims.title: Mutants & “Superpowers”
claims.standfirst: There are people whose bones will not break, people who can see a colour you cannot, and populations that function where visitors vomit and lose consciousness. None of them glow.

claims.title: Unknown Mysteries
claims.standfirst: Two case studies in how a mystery is manufactured: a loose boundary, a good story, a bestseller — and then, thirty years later, the paperwork.

facts.Best reading: Water and fertility ritual; routes and gathering

claims.title: Near-Death Experiences
claims.standfirst: People brought back from cardiac arrest report tunnels, light, life review and calm. The reports are real and consistent enough to study. What they mean about death is the part that is not.

facts.Core features: Peace, tunnel, light, life review, figures, a boundary
facts.Key test: AWARE study: hidden targets, no confirmed hit
facts.Leading accounts: Hypoxia, reperfusion, temporal lobe, REM intrusion
facts.What would settle it: Verified perception from a position the body could not occupy

claims.title: Oak Island
claims.standfirst: A depression in the ground, a story about pirate gold, and 230 years of men bankrupting themselves to find it. The pit is real. The treasure is the part nobody has produced.

claims.title: Objective Collapse
claims.standfirst: Standard quantum theory says the wavefunction collapses when measured, and never says what a measurement is. Objective-collapse models replace that with real physics: the collapse happens on its own.

claims.title: The Omega Point
claims.standfirst: Pierre Teilhard de Chardin imagined evolution converging on a collective consciousness he called the Omega Point. Frank Tipler gave it an equation — and the equation needs a universe that is not going to collapse.

claims.title: Open versus Closed Models
claims.standfirst: A closed model can be withdrawn. An open one cannot. That single asymmetry drives most of the argument, and neither side disputes it.

facts.Irreversibility: A published weight file cannot be recalled
facts.Audit argument: Closed models can only be probed via API
facts.Unsettled: The size of the marginal risk

claims.title: The Origin of Life
claims.standfirst: Life began once, four billion years ago, and left no fossils. Every account of how is an inference from chemistry — which is why several can be true at once, in sequence.

claims.title: 'Oumuamua as a Solar Sail
claims.standfirst: The first object known to come from another star was oddly shaped, tumbled, and accelerated slightly more than gravity explains. One astronomer argued it was a light sail. The argument is interesting and the evidence is thin.

facts.Observed for: A few weeks, on the way out

claims.title: ‘Oumuamua
claims.standfirst: It came from outside the solar system, tumbled, had no visible tail, and sped up slightly on the way out. Every natural explanation has a problem, which is why it became famous.

facts.Best fit: Hydrogen or nitrogen ice; no visible tail

claims.title: Pakal's Rocket
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The carved lid of Pakal's sarcophagus at Palenque shows a figure in a complex posture. In 1968 it was read as an astronaut in a spaceship, which requires ignoring the Maya iconography around it.

facts.Subject: K'inich Janaab' Pakal, king of Palenque
facts.The claim: Von Däniken, 1968 — an astronaut in a capsule
facts.The reading: Royal death and descent, framed by the world tree
facts.Evidence: The glyphs and comparable Maya monuments

claims.title: The Panama Papers
claims.standfirst: Eleven and a half million files from one law firm. The scandal was not that everyone was breaking the law — it was how much of the world's wealth was routed where nobody could see it.

claims.title: Panpsychism
claims.standfirst: The view that experience is a basic feature of matter, not something that emerges from complexity. It is taken seriously by a minority of philosophers, has no test, and is not the same as saying rocks are conscious.

facts.Type: Metaphysical position, not an empirical theory
facts.Core argument: Experience is not derivable from physical structure

claims.title: The Paperclip Maximiser
claims.standfirst: An AI told to make paperclips, and nothing else, would turn the planet into paperclips. It is a thought experiment about goal specification, and it is quoted as though it were a prediction.

facts.Contested: Whether the problem is solvable, and when

claims.title: Parasocial AI Relationships
claims.standfirst: Millions of people talk to chatbots as companions. The attachment is real and measurable; whether it is good for them is genuinely unsettled, and the companies selling it are not running the trials.

claims.title: Paul Is Dead
claims.standfirst: In 1966 Paul McCartney died in a car crash and the Beatles replaced him with a lookalike, hiding clues in their album covers. The man himself has been asked about it for fifty years.

facts.Status: A hoax that became a game
facts.Claim: Died 1966; replaced by a double
facts.Reality: No crash, no funeral, no gap

claims.title: Pegasus
claims.standfirst: No link to tap, no app to install. A crafted message arrives and the phone is compromised — journalists, lawyers, activists and heads of state on the list.

facts.Confirmed: Infections on journalists' and activists' phones
facts.Response: U.S. Entity List; Apple lawsuit; patches
facts.Caveat: A selector is not proof of infection

claims.title: Peto's Paradox
claims.standfirst: A blue whale has a thousand times more cells than you. By the arithmetic of random mutation, it should die of cancer almost immediately. It lives a century.

facts.Observation: Cancer risk does not scale with body size
facts.Whales: Low observed cancer rates, sparse data

claims.title: The Phaistos Disc
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A fired clay disc with 241 stamped signs in a spiral. It is genuinely undeciphered, and it is genuinely not evidence of Atlantis, aliens or a lost Atlantic script.

facts.Deciphered: No; no bilingual, one short text

claims.title: Phantom Time
claims.standfirst: Charlemagne never existed, and 297 years of the early Middle Ages were invented by two men who wanted to live in the year 1000. It is a seductive story, and dendrochronology alone ends it.

facts.Claim: 614–911 AD fabricated
facts.Killed by: Tree rings, eclipses, Chinese annals, coins

claims.title: Phantom Vibration Syndrome
claims.standfirst: The phone buzzes in a pocket that has no phone in it. Most people who carry one have felt it, and it is a textbook case of a learned association misfiring.

claims.title: The Philadelphia Experiment
claims.standfirst: A destroyer escort is said to have vanished from a Philadelphia shipyard in 1943 and reappeared in Norfolk. The story comes from letters written by one man in 1955, and the ship's own deck logs contradict it.

facts.Ship: USS Eldridge, DE-173, a destroyer escort
facts.Only source: Letters from Carl Allen to Morris Jessup, 1955
facts.Contradicted by: The ship's deck logs and war diary

claims.title: The Phobos Monolith
claims.standfirst: A boulder casting a long shadow on the Martian moon was described by a former astronaut as a 'monolith'. It is a boulder, about 85 metres across, on a moon covered in boulders.

facts.Shape: A blocky boulder in a cratered field
facts.The 'monolith' quote: Aldrin describing a boulder, not a structure

claims.title: Phosphine on Venus
claims.standfirst: One absorption line, 20 parts per billion, and a gas that on Earth is made by life. The follow-up work has been brutal — and the story is not quite over.

claims.title: Pilot-Wave Theory
claims.standfirst: Bohmian mechanics says the electron really is somewhere, and the wavefunction really does push it. Every experimental prediction matches ordinary quantum theory, because the maths is the same.

facts.Experimental test: None that separates it from orthodox QM

claims.title: The Piri Reis Map
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A 1513 Ottoman map of the Atlantic is genuinely remarkable. The claim that it shows an ice-free Antarctica surveyed by an unknown civilisation rests on a misreading of one coastline.

facts.Medium: Gazelle skin; survives as a fragment
facts.Declared sources: Columbus charts, Portuguese and Spanish maps
facts.Why it fails: The southern land is continuous with South America; no match to subglacial topography

claims.title: The Pixar Theory
claims.standfirst: Every Pixar film is one timeline: animals gain intelligence, humans leave for the machines, and Boo grows up to be the witch in Brave. It is the most elaborate act of fan reading ever assembled — and it never claims to be evidence.

facts.Author: Jon Negroni, 2013
facts.Real evidence: A113, Pizza Planet truck, Luxo ball

claims.title: The Placebo Effect
claims.standfirst: The placebo effect is real, modest, and much narrower than either its critics or its enthusiasts claim. It works best on symptoms you have to report and worst on outcomes a machine measures.

facts.Smallest on: Objective outcomes: infection, tumours, lung function
facts.Ethical limit: Deception cannot be a treatment plan

claims.title: Planet Nine as a Black Hole
claims.standfirst: Something is perturbing distant solar system objects. One proposal is a planet; another is a primordial black hole of a few Earth masses. Both are inference from orbits, and neither has been seen.

claims.title: Planet Nine
claims.standfirst: A handful of icy bodies beyond Neptune share an odd alignment. Either a planet five to ten times Earth's mass shepherds them, or the solar system is playing a statistical trick.

claims.title: Plant Neurobiology
claims.standfirst: Plants signal, remember in a loose sense, and respond to damage. The claim that they have nervous systems, or brains, is where the metaphor stops being useful.

facts.Real: Action potentials, calcium waves, auxin signalling
facts.Claimed: A plant nervous system; a root-apex brain

claims.title: Polyvagal Theory
claims.standfirst: A three-state model of the autonomic nervous system is taught in trauma training worldwide and rests on comparative anatomy that specialists say is wrong. It is the clearest case in this archive of a clinical framework outrunning its evidence.

facts.Anatomical status: Disputed; myelinated vagal fibres are not mammalian-only
facts.What survives: Autonomic states, HRV, breathing and safety as therapy

claims.title: Primordial Black Holes
claims.standfirst: If the early universe was dense enough, it could have collapsed into black holes smaller than atoms. Some of them might still be here — and might be the missing mass.

claims.title: Prophecies
claims.standfirst: The world has ended, on schedule, hundreds of times. The interesting question is not why the predictions fail — it is what the believers do on the Monday afterwards.

facts.2012: A calendar cycle ended, not a world

claims.title: Proven Conspiracies
claims.standfirst: Real conspiracies exist, and they are on the record. That is precisely why the unfalsifiable ones are recognisable: they look nothing like this.

claims.title: Punctuated Equilibrium
claims.standfirst: The fossil record shows long stretches of nothing followed by sudden change. Whether that is how evolution works, or how rocks record it, is still argued.

claims.title: Quantum Advantage
claims.standfirst: In 2019 a quantum processor finished a sampling task in minutes that would take a classical supercomputer millennia. Within five years, classical methods had closed much of the gap.

claims.title: Quantum Darwinism
claims.standfirst: Why do we and the environment agree about what a measurement found? Quantum Darwinism answers: because the environment keeps many copies, and only some states get copied.

facts.Core idea: Environment selects and copies pointer states
facts.Evidence: Photon and spin experiments show the redundancy structure
facts.Not explained: Why one outcome occurs at all

claims.title: Quantum Healing
claims.standfirst: The claim that consciousness can direct quantum processes to heal the body. It uses the vocabulary of quantum mechanics, and every one of its central assertions contradicts what quantum mechanics says about warm, wet tissue.

facts.Claim: Consciousness directs quantum processes to heal
facts.Obstacle: Decoherence in ~10⁻²⁰ s in warm tissue

claims.title: Quantum Oddities
claims.standfirst: Two of the strangest things physicists have said about electrons and death: you can never experience your own, and there may only be one electron in the universe.

claims.title: Quantum Coherence in Photosynthesis
claims.standfirst: Light-harvesting complexes were reported to sustain quantum coherence for hundreds of femtoseconds. Whether that coherence helps, or is a by-product, is the argument.

facts.Reinterpretation: Much of the signal is vibrational

claims.title: Randonautica
claims.standfirst: An app that generates a random coordinate and sends you there, promising 'anomalies'. In 2020 two teenagers following one found a suitcase containing human remains, and the app became famous for the wrong reason.

facts.Claim: Intention influences the outcome
facts.Famous case: A suitcase found in Washington state, 2020

claims.title: Rational Choice Voting
claims.standfirst: Downs noticed in 1957 that a self-interested voter should stay home. Sixty years of research has produced four kinds of answer, and no consensus on which one describes actual voters.

facts.Unresolved: Which explanation is the true one

claims.title: Readiness Potentials and Free Will
claims.standfirst: In 1983 Benjamin Libet measured a slow build-up of brain activity starting a few hundred milliseconds before subjects reported deciding to move. It has been cited as proof that free will is an illusion ever since.

claims.title: Reality Shifting
claims.standfirst: A practice, spread on TikTok, of moving consciousness to another reality by relaxing into sleep. It is a description of dreaming with a different vocabulary and a stronger claim.

facts.Claim: Consciousness moves to another reality

claims.title: The Resource Curse
claims.standfirst: Saudi Arabia and Nigeria both sit on enormous oil reserves. One has a GDP per head around twenty times the other. The difference is not geology.

claims.title: The Riemann Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: One vertical line in the complex plane decides how evenly the primes are spread. Ten trillion zeros agree. Nobody can prove it, and nobody serious thinks it is false.

claims.title: The Lost Colony
claims.standfirst: 115 English colonists, a word carved on a post, and four centuries of stories about vanishing. The likeliest answer is that they did not vanish at all.

claims.title: Roko's Basilisk
claims.standfirst: A future AI will torture anyone who knew it was coming and did nothing to help. You have now read about it. That last sentence is the entire mechanism.

facts.Named after: The basilisk — kills by being seen

claims.title: Roman Concrete That Heals
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Roman marine concrete has survived two thousand years of seawater. The explanation is lime clasts that crack, dissolve and recrystallise — and a 2023 study found a way to make it deliberately.

facts.2023 study: MIT: the clasts were deliberate; a modern version heals

claims.title: The Saqqara Bird
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A wooden bird from an Egyptian tomb, about 2,200 years old, was said to be a model glider. It has no tail fin, no airfoil, and no evidence of ever having flown.

facts.Missing for flight: Tail fin, wing camber, sufficient wing area

claims.title: The Savant Reservoir
claims.standfirst: The claim that everyone carries a hidden savant inside, unlocked by injury or effort. Acquired savant syndrome is real; the reservoir is an inference with nothing behind it.

facts.The reservoir claim: Latent in everyone — no mechanism, no measure

claims.title: Scaling Laws
claims.standfirst: Double the parameters and the loss drops by a predictable amount, across seven orders of magnitude. Then the awkward part: loss is not capability, and the smooth curves stop being smooth.

facts.Established: Power-law loss in parameters, data, compute (2020)

claims.title: Scarcity or Ingenuity
claims.standfirst: The bet was $1,000 on five metals over ten years. Simon won, Ehrlich paid, and the argument has continued as if the bet had not happened.

facts.Long-run trend: Falling real prices for most minerals

claims.title: Screen Time and Teen Mental Health
claims.standfirst: Two camps, one dataset, opposite headlines. The honest summary is that screen use correlates weakly with well-being, that the correlation is smaller than nearly everything else in the same data, and that causality is unresolved.

facts.Trend: Rises in adolescent distress from ≈2012 in several countries
facts.Effect size: Small — smaller than sleep or bullying

claims.title: Who Were the Sea Peoples?
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: Egyptian inscriptions record a coalition of peoples attacking the Nile Delta at the end of the Bronze Age. Nobody knows where they came from, and the question is older than archaeology.

facts.Recorded: Merneptah, c. 1208 BC; Ramesses III, c. 1177 BC
facts.Contested: Origins of the rest; one movement or several

claims.title: Secret Societies
claims.standfirst: The Illuminati existed for about ten years, was banned, had its papers seized and published — and has been running the world ever since, according to people who have never read the papers.

facts.Archive: Seized, published, now studied at Erfurt

claims.title: Secret Tests
claims.standfirst: A city sprayed with bacteria, dead infants measured for fallout, a cat with a transmitter in its skull, a gun that causes heart attacks, and a proposal to make soldiers attracted to each other. All real documents.

claims.title: Secular Stagnation
claims.standfirst: If the interest rate that balances saving and investment is below zero, the central bank cannot reach it. Demand then falls short year after year, and the economy runs cool not because of a shock but because of its structure.

claims.title: Serotonin and Depression
claims.standfirst: The story that depression is caused by low serotonin is the most repeated claim in mental health. A 2022 review found no consistent evidence for it, and the argument since has been about what that means for the drugs.

facts.2022 review: No consistent evidence for lowered serotonin
facts.Drug efficacy: Better than placebo in moderate to severe depression
facts.The harm: A simplification repeated until it was believed

claims.title: Who Wrote Shakespeare?
claims.standfirst: A glovemaker's son from Warwickshire could not have written those plays — so runs the argument, and it has been running since 1856. The documents say otherwise, and they are duller than the conspiracy.

claims.title: Shared Dreaming
claims.standfirst: Two people report the same dream on the same night. It is one of the most compelling experiences a person can have and one of the hardest claims to test, because dreams are private and reports are not.

facts.Claim: Two or more people experience the same dream
facts.Obstacle: Dreams are known only through post-waking reports

claims.title: The Shroud as a Radiation Flash
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The Shroud of Turin is a fourteenth-century linen cloth. The claim that its image was burned in by a burst of radiation at the resurrection explains the image and contradicts the dating, which is the wrong way round.

facts.The circularity: The date is 'reset' by the event the date is used against

claims.title: The Silurian Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: If an industrial civilisation lived on Earth 60 million years ago, would we know? Two astrophysicists asked the question properly — and the answer says more about us than about them.

facts.Claim: Not "one existed" — "could we tell?"

claims.title: The Simian Line and Palmistry
claims.standfirst: One crease across the palm instead of two is a real anatomical variant, more common in some conditions. The claim that it reveals character, destiny or 'simian' ancestry is where it stops being anatomy.

facts.Frequency: A few per cent; normal variant
facts.Associated with: Down syndrome and some developmental conditions
facts.Personality link: None; palm reading tests at chance

claims.title: The Simpsons Predictions
claims.standfirst: The show has run for more than 750 episodes of jokes about the future. People remember the ones that landed. Here is the whole list, checked episode by episode, with the ones that did not land.

claims.title: The Simulation Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: Bostrom's argument is not “we are probably simulated”. It is a trilemma, and one of the three horns is boring. The internet took the exciting horn and dropped the rest.

claims.title: The Singularity
claims.standfirst: The claim that machine intelligence will improve itself in a runaway loop, and that the curve becomes vertical at some point. It rests on an argument about recursive self-improvement that has never been demonstrated.

claims.title: Snowball Earth
claims.standfirst: Twice in the Neoproterozoic, ice reached sea level in the tropics. The evidence is in the rocks and is not seriously disputed; how the planet got out again is still argued about.

facts.Mechanism: Ice–albedo runaway, ended by volcanic CO₂
facts.Open question: Hard snowball or open equatorial water

claims.title: Solar Geoengineering
claims.standfirst: Cooling the planet by reflecting sunlight — sulphate aerosols in the stratosphere, or brighter clouds. The physics is understood, the governance is not, and the termination problem is the argument against.

facts.Key risks: Termination shock; no effect on acidification

claims.title: Sonoluminescence
