claims.standfirst: Sound makes a bubble collapse; the collapse emits a flash of light lasting picoseconds. The inside may be hotter than the surface of the Sun, and nobody can measure it directly.

claims.title: The Electromagnetic Soul
claims.standfirst: “The soul is an electromagnetic pattern; the body is hardware.” It sounds like physics. It is a metaphor wearing a lab coat — and the real measurements are more interesting than the metaphor.

facts.Fatal step: Fields are a product, not the mind

claims.title: The Space Elevator
claims.standfirst: Tsiolkovsky proposed it in 1895 after seeing the Eiffel Tower. Arthur C. Clarke made it famous in 1979. It remains the cheapest imaginable way to orbit and the least available, for one reason: the material.

claims.title: Water Erosion on the Sphinx
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The Sphinx's enclosure shows deep vertical weathering. Whether that pattern is rain, salt, wind or groundwater decides how old the monument is, and the argument has been running since 1979.

facts.Claim: Rainfall erosion implies an older date
facts.Mainstream reading: Salt exfoliation, wind, groundwater, joint-controlled fissures
facts.Complication: Centuries of burial, excavation and repair
facts.What would settle it: A survey separating original surface from repairs

claims.title: The Splinternet
claims.standfirst: The internet is fragmenting into national and regional blocs, with different rules, different infrastructure and different content. It is measurable, and the measurement is the interesting part.

claims.title: Split-Brain Consciousness
claims.standfirst: Severing the connection between the hemispheres produced patients whose two halves seemed to know different things. Whether that means two minds is still argued.

claims.title: Stochastic Parrots or World Models
claims.standfirst: One camp says a language model is a curve-fitting machine that parrots its training data. The other says that to predict text well enough, it has to build a model of the world that produced it.

facts.Strongest evidence for structure: Board-state probes in chess and Othello models
facts.Open question: How general the learned representations are

claims.title: The Stoned Ape
claims.standfirst: Human brains tripled in size because our ancestors ate psilocybin mushrooms, which rewired us into language, art and self-reflection. It is a wonderful story with a real pharmacology and almost no archaeology.

claims.title: Stonehenge Acoustics
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A replica of Stonehenge has been built and measured. The stones do affect sound in ways that would matter for speech, music and drumming — and the site is a ruin, which is the problem with every claim about how it sounded.

facts.The problem: The site is a ruin; reconstructions differ
facts.Unresolved: Whether any acoustic effect was intended

claims.title: Stonehenge as a Computer
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: In 1963 an astronomer argued that Stonehenge was a machine for predicting eclipses. The alignments are real; the machine is the part that did not survive scrutiny.

facts.Claim: An observatory and an eclipse predictor
facts.Problem: 165 points produce thousands of chance alignments

claims.title: Strings versus Loops
claims.standfirst: Two research programmes, one target: a theory of gravity that works at the Planck scale. They disagree about almost everything else, and neither has been tested.

claims.title: Substrate Independence
claims.standfirst: Functionalism says a mind is defined by what it does, not what it is made of — so the same program would be conscious wherever it ran. That is either obvious or a category error, and the disagreement is about which.

claims.title: Dual Suns, Dual Stars
claims.standfirst: The Sun has no companion today. That is a measurement, not an opinion — and yet the “second sun” idea is one of the most persistent in fringe cosmology, because it is half right.

claims.title: Room-Temperature Superconductivity
claims.standfirst: A material that carries current with no resistance would rebuild the electrical grid. The physics is real; the room-temperature claims have not survived.

claims.title: Superrationality
claims.standfirst: In a one-shot prisoner's dilemma with a stranger, defecting is dominant. Unless the stranger is your mirror — in which case the choice is not what to do, but what kind of reasoner to be.

facts.Key assumption: Both players run the same reasoning
facts.Descendants: Evidential, timeless and functional decision theory

claims.title: Supersymmetry
claims.standfirst: A symmetry between matter and force particles would solve several problems at once. The LHC was built partly to find it, and has found nothing. That is not the same as ruling it out.

claims.title: Jung's Synchronicity
claims.standfirst: A meaningful coincidence with no causal connection, offered as an acausal principle of nature. The concept names something people experience; as a claim about the world it cannot be tested, which is the problem.

facts.Testability: None — meaning is assigned after the fact
facts.Base rate: Coincidences are common; that is arithmetic

claims.title: Synesthesia
claims.standfirst: For some people, letters have colours and sounds have tastes, consistently, for a lifetime. It is one of the few claims in this archive that a laboratory can check in an afternoon.

facts.Mechanism: Contested; reduced neonatal pruning is the leading account

claims.title: Tabby’s Star
claims.standfirst: A star 1,470 light years away keeps dimming in strange, uneven ways. A comet swarm was the first guess, dust the current one — and a megastructure was never more than a headline.

claims.title: Tardigrades Between Planets
claims.standfirst: A millimetre-long animal that survives vacuum, radiation and decades without water is real. The claim built on top of it — that life travels between planets — is a different proposition, and the experiments that get quoted do not support it.

facts.Tun state: Metabolism below measurement; DNA repaired on rehydration
facts.Space test: 2007, low Earth orbit, ten days, survivors
facts.Panspermia: Not demonstrated; the transit dose is the problem

claims.title: Tartaria & the Mud Flood
claims.standfirst: Every old city has basement windows cut in half by the pavement. The theory says a civilisation of giants built the buildings, then a wall of mud buried the ground floors and the history books.

facts.“Tartary” in fact: European label for inner Asia — not an empire
facts.Core evidence: Buried ground floors, fair buildings, star forts
facts.Real explanation: Street regrading, temporary exhibition halls, bastion geometry

claims.title: Tartarus, the Pit
claims.standfirst: “As far beneath the earth as heaven is above it.” The Greeks gave the underworld a floor plan, a wall, a gate and a prisoner list. Everything after that is reuse.

facts.Depth: Nine days and nights of falling
facts.Inmates: The Titans; Typhoeus; later, human sinners

claims.title: Technofeudalism
claims.standfirst: The claim that cloud platforms have replaced markets with rents, and that capitalism has been succeeded by something older in structure. It is a thesis about political economy, argued from data that is contested.

facts.Claim: Cloud platforms extract rent; capitalism has been succeeded
facts.Contested: Rent versus profit as the description
facts.Missing: Evidence that a new mode of production exists

claims.title: Technological Unemployment
claims.standfirst: Every generation has been told that machines will end work, and every generation has been mostly wrong. That history is an argument, not a guarantee.

facts.Current AI evidence: Task-level gains; no clear aggregate effect yet
facts.Key variable: Whether new tasks are created for people

claims.title: Earth Was Terraformed
claims.standfirst: The claim that Earth was engineered for life — by an earlier civilisation, or by design. It borrows the language of a real scientific debate about fine-tuning and rare Earth, and then adds an agent nobody has evidence for.

facts.Claim: Earth was engineered for life

claims.title: The Tetris Effect
claims.standfirst: Play Tetris for hours and the falling blocks follow you into sleep and into the shower. The effect is real, it has a name, and it turned out to be a window on how memory consolidates.

facts.Finding: Imagery at sleep onset, in most intensive players

claims.title: Theranos
claims.standfirst: One drop of blood, two hundred tests, a black box. The machine did not work, the tests ran on other companies' equipment, and the board did not include a single haematologist.

facts.Claim: 200+ tests from one drop of blood
facts.Reality: Few tests; most run on commercial analysers

claims.title: The Thucydides Trap
claims.standfirst: Thucydides said the war between Athens and Sparta came from 'the growth of Athenian power and the fear this caused in Sparta'. Allison turned that sentence into a dataset.

claims.title: Time Crystals
claims.standfirst: An ordinary crystal repeats in space. A time crystal repeats in time, indefinitely, without consuming energy — and unlike a pendulum, it does so in its ground state.

facts.Driven?: Yes — a discrete time crystal needs a drive

claims.title: Time Paradoxes
claims.standfirst: Kill your grandfather and you were never born; travel back and give yourself the idea you got from yourself. These paradoxes are not puzzles about fiction. They are what happens when you take the equations of relativity seriously.

claims.title: Timewave Zero
claims.standfirst: A curve derived from the I Ching, claimed to map the novelty of the universe and to end in 2012. The date passed; the curve was fitted, not derived.

facts.Basis: The King Wen sequence of the I Ching
facts.Outcome: No event; no revision into a testable claim
facts.Method: A curve with free parameters, fitted to history

claims.title: Tired Light
claims.standfirst: Redshift could be caused by photons losing energy on the way, rather than by the expansion of space. It was a serious alternative for sixty years, and three measurements have closed it.

facts.Claim: Redshift is photon energy loss in transit
facts.Killed by: Time dilation, the CMB, surface brightness
facts.Why it persists: It would remove the Big Bang

claims.title: Tulpas
claims.standfirst: A practice imported from Tibetan Buddhism and rebuilt on internet forums: deliberately create a second mind in your head, and talk to it. The reports are real; the claim that there is a second mind is not testable.

facts.Reports: A voice with its own opinions; sometimes distress

claims.title: Turbulence
claims.standfirst: We can land a rocket on a barge using models of turbulent flow. We cannot prove that the equations describing it always have smooth solutions.

claims.title: The Turing Test
claims.standfirst: Turing's 1950 paper replaced an unanswerable question with a game: can a machine's text be told from a person's? Seventy-five years later the game is won and the original question is exactly where it was.

facts.Turing's prediction: Machine fools an average interrogator by ≈2000
facts.What it tests: Fluency and human modelling, not understanding

claims.title: Tutankhamun's Meteorite Dagger
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A dagger buried with Tutankhamun was made of iron that fell from the sky. It took ninety years and an X-ray fluorescence spectrometer to prove what the nickel content had hinted at.

facts.Significance: Iron before the Iron Age came from meteorites

claims.title: Underwater Worlds
claims.standfirst: More than two-thirds of the seafloor has no modern high-resolution map. That single fact powers an industry of undersea-civilization claims — and it is also the most honest fact on this page.

facts.Related: Inner oceans, Lake monsters, Bermuda Triangle

claims.title: Unexplained Phenomena
claims.standfirst: The honest cases. Not ghosts and not cover-ups — events with real evidence, real papers, and conclusions that are still argued.

claims.title: Universal Basic Income
claims.standfirst: The strongest argument for a basic income is not that it makes people work more. It is that a welfare state built on conditions and paperwork produces the poverty it claims to fix.

facts.Trials: Finland, Kenya, Stockton, Denver, and dozens more
facts.Employment effect: Small in most trials; not the collapse predicted

claims.title: Urban Legends & Creepypasta
claims.standfirst: A Photoshop contest produced a monster. Five years later, two twelve-year-olds tried to kill their friend for him. This is the only page in the archive where the fiction caused the harm.

claims.title: Life in Venus's Clouds
claims.standfirst: The surface of Venus is hot enough to melt lead. Fifty kilometres up, the pressure and temperature are almost Earth-like — which is why the cloud layer keeps being proposed as a habitat, and why the phosphine claim of 2020 mattered.

facts.Droplets: 75–96% sulfuric acid; very low water activity
facts.Reanalysis: SO₂ and artefacts; abundance at most a trace

claims.title: The Vinland Map
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: A fifteenth-century map showing Vinland looked like proof that the Norse reached America before Columbus. The ink turned out to contain a pigment that was not manufactured until the 1920s.

facts.Decisive finding: Anatase (TiO₂) in the industrial form, in the ink
facts.Norse contact: Still established — by L'Anse aux Meadows

claims.title: Where Viruses Came From
claims.standfirst: Viruses are not alive by most definitions, and they are the most abundant biological entities on Earth. Where they came from is one of biology's genuinely unresolved questions.

claims.title: The Voynich Manuscript
claims.standfirst: An illustrated book in an unknown script, written on vellum dated to the early fifteenth century. Every generation produces a decipherment. None has survived contact with other scholars.

claims.title: Where Earth’s Water Came From
claims.standfirst: Oceans cover most of the planet, and the planet should have boiled them off while it was forming. Something delivered water afterwards — or it was here all along.

claims.title: The Wet-Bulb Threshold
claims.standfirst: At a wet-bulb temperature of about 35 °C, sweat stops cooling the body and a healthy adult dies within hours, even in the shade. It is a hard physical limit, and parts of the world are approaching it.

facts.Mechanism: Sweat can no longer cool the skin

claims.title: Whale Strandings
claims.standfirst: Hundreds of whales beach themselves together, and the explanations on offer range from sonar to solar storms. Some of them have been demonstrated. Most have not.

facts.Commonest species: Pilot whales, sperm whales, beaked whales
facts.Social mechanism: Pod cohesion: one animal's error becomes the group's
facts.Key evidence: Necropsy: gas-bubble lesions in exposed beaked whales

claims.title: White Holes
claims.standfirst: Run the film backwards and a black hole becomes a white hole: a region nothing can enter, spraying matter outward. The equations permit it. The sky has not shown one.

claims.title: Why We Age
claims.standfirst: Ageing is not one process. Several mechanisms are well described, no single one explains it, and the interventions that extend lifespan in mice have mostly failed to translate.

facts.Evolutionary accounts: Mutation accumulation; antagonistic pleiotropy; disposable soma
facts.Mechanistic hallmarks: Nine, including senescence and proteostasis loss
facts.Interventions: Caloric restriction, rapamycin, senolytics — under study

claims.title: Why We Dream
claims.standfirst: Dreams are vivid, emotional, remembered badly, and unexplained. The leading theories disagree about whether they do anything at all.

facts.Theories: Activation-synthesis; threat simulation; memory; social simulation
facts.Documented: REM association; incorporation of recent experience
facts.Limitation: Content known only from waking reports

claims.title: Why We Sleep
claims.standfirst: Sleep restores something, and after a century of research nobody can say precisely what. The candidates are all supported and none is sufficient.

facts.Necessary: Yes; deprivation is harmful and eventually fatal
facts.Candidate functions: Restoration, synaptic homeostasis, clearance, immunity, safety

claims.title: Why We Yawn
claims.standfirst: Yawning is contagious, appears before birth, and has no agreed function. The brain-cooling account is the best supported; the social account explains the contagion.

claims.title: The Wow! Signal
claims.standfirst: Seventy-two seconds of narrowband radio at the hydrogen frequency, recorded once and never again. It is still the best candidate for a signal from elsewhere, and it is not evidence of one.

claims.title: Xenotransplantation
claims.standfirst: Transplanting pig organs into people. The first living recipients survived weeks to months, which is both a real advance and a long way from a treatment.

claims.title: Yamashita's Gold
claims.theme: The ancient world, myth and archaeology
claims.standfirst: The claim that the Japanese army buried billions in looted treasure in the Philippines at the end of the war. Seventy years of digging has produced plaques, tunnels and lawsuits, and no gold.

facts.Claim: Billions in looted treasure buried in the Philippines
facts.Not documented: The hoard, its size, the maps

claims.title: The Younger Dryas Impact
claims.standfirst: The Younger Dryas cooling is real and abrupt. Whether an impact caused it — and whether that impact explains megafaunal extinctions and the Clovis collapse — is where the argument starts.

claims.title: Why Zebras Have Stripes
claims.standfirst: Camouflage, confusion, cooling and social signalling have all been proposed. The hypothesis with the best experimental support is the least romantic one: flies.

facts.Experiment: Striped horse coats, 2019 and 2023: fewer landings
facts.Consensus: Probably several mechanisms, with flies first

claims.title: The Zoo Hypothesis
claims.standfirst: If the galaxy is full of life, why is it quiet? John Ball's 1973 answer was that they are leaving us alone on purpose — treating Earth as a preserve, and waiting for us to grow up.
